rule: GOAL: Navigate the grid maze to reach the green target cell using the shortest path. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one cell per press, consuming one unit from the step timer. RULE: The timer counts down from sixty-four, requiring an efficient route to arrive before time expires. TRAP: Assuming the timer is infinite or irrelevant leads to wandering and failure, as every move costs time.

GOAL: Guide the falling ball into a specific cup gap by positioning the paddle correctly. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide the paddle horizontally; Space executes the move and triggers the physics simulation. RULE: The paddle must be positioned so the ball bounces into the cup’s opening, not onto the rim or floor. TRAP: Assuming the paddle simply catches the ball stops progress; it actually deflects the trajectory based on impact point.

GOAL: Guide the key through the wall gap to the exit. CONTROLS: Clicking the upper blue block moves the key right; clicking the lower blue block moves it left. RULE: The vertical position of your click relative to the wall determines the movement direction. TRAP: Clicking the key or empty space does nothing; only the blue side blocks are interactive.

GOAL: Guide the floating block into the matching socket below. CONTROLS: Toggle switches to set movement direction and distance, then activate the lever to execute the path. RULE: The block must align perfectly with the socket’s indentations to complete the circuit. TRAP: Assuming a single long move works; precise, incremental steps are often needed to avoid collision with the rim.

GOAL: Guide a robot to slot three colored blocks into matching receptacles. CONTROLS: Arrows move the robot; Space grabs or releases the block directly in front. RULE: The robot automatically faces the direction of movement, determining which block it interacts with. TRAP: Assuming you can rotate while carrying a block to change its position relative to the robot.

GOAL: Guide the sliding token to touch the glowing ball at the top of the rail. CONTROLS: Click any spot on the rail to instantly slide the token to that position. RULE: The token travels in straight lines along the track, ignoring intermediate obstacles. TRAP: Thinking you need to step through every marked dot; you can jump directly to the target.

GOAL: Unfold the zigzag gray strip to reveal the hidden path. CONTROLS: Click blue blocks above or below walls to shift the strip segments left or right. RULE: The strip’s total length is constant, so extending one arm shortens another. TRAP: Treating the strip as separate arms instead of one continuous folded piece caused wasted moves.

GOAL: Extend two bars to touch their target markers. CONTROLS: Click glyphs to move the bar’s far end; pointing away extends, pointing toward shrinks. RULE: Each click shifts the bar’s end by three units in the glyph’s direction. TRAP: Assuming the near end moves; only the far end changes position, leaving the base fixed.

GOAL: Align the pink symbols with their blue partners using a shared rotation cycle. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor between slots; UP or DOWN rotates the current symbol. RULE: Each slot’s target is determined by the blue symbol above it via a fixed modular offset. TRAP: Assuming UP always increases value regardless of the current position in the cycle.

GOAL: Align three plugs by balancing material across five connected pockets to specific target heights. CONTROLS: Click left or right buttons on each wall to transfer two units of material into the adjacent pocket. RULE: Material cannot spill over the lower of two adjacent walls, strictly limiting each pocket's maximum capacity. TRAP: Assuming pockets act as independent containers fails; you must constantly move material through tight central pockets to avoid overflow.

GOAL: Shrink the key tip to a 2x2 block so it fits through the narrow channel and slides into the head. CONTROLS: Click keypad cells to consume key material. Use arrow keys to slide the remaining tip left or right. RULE: The passage between the head and shaft is only two rows tall; the tip must be no larger than this to pass. TRAP: Trying to force the full-sized tip into the slot; you must first reduce its height by clicking away excess cells.

GOAL: Reach the exit while avoiding the red predator's lethal lunge. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move your character one cell in that direction. RULE: You survive only if you never occupy the same cell as the predator after its turn. TRAP: Believing landing on the enemy triggers a safe swap; it actually causes immediate death.

GOAL: Merge two tokens by moving them until they overlap. CONTROLS: Click a spot to slide a token toward it, stopping if another token blocks the path. RULE: Tokens only move if the target is within their specific range, measured from the token's edge. TRAP: Assuming you must click the exact destination; clicking any spot in range moves the token to the limit or blocker.

GOAL: Shrink the large tip into a small block and pass it through the gate. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block; clicking white cells triggers the shrink. RULE: The remaining block is always the top-left quadrant of the original tip. TRAP: You might think you need to align the tip before shrinking, but you can nudge the small block horizontally after it forms.

ESTABLISHED: The rod extends to push blocks right when aligned. FAILED: Extending the rod while the target block is in its path pushes the block sideways instead of setting up a vertical move. GOAL IS NOT: Simply extending the rod to maximum length at the target block's current row. CONTROLS: Extending the rod pushes blocks in the extension direction; moving the head vertically sweeps the rod against blocks in its column range.

GOAL: Move the green cap to the target zone by adjusting the height of the sky and yellow bands. CONTROLS: Clicking a panel's right cell expands that color's vertical block, pushing stacked layers upward or sideways. RULE: Expanding a lower layer lifts everything above it; expanding an upper layer only grows its own size. TRAP: Thinking growth is independent; ignoring that sky expansion raises the yellow band, which then carries the green cap.

GOAL: Clear the path by eating three monsters in a specific order to avoid getting cornered. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move one step; landing on a monster consumes it. RULE: Monsters only lunge if you are adjacent in the direction they face, not just any nearby square. TRAP: Assuming any adjacent monster attacks regardless of orientation, causing you to waste moves avoiding safe squares.

GOAL: Move all pieces to their matching goal circles. CONTROLS: Click empty space to push the nearest piece. RULE: Pieces merge if they collide; only single pieces reach goals. TRAP: Clicking too close to multiple pieces causes accidental merges.

GOAL: Match the top reference row exactly by placing colored blocks into the bottom slots. CONTROLS: Click a color in the palette to select it, then click a slot to place it. RULE: The top row displays the required color order; the bottom slots must mirror this sequence. TRAP: Assuming the top row was merely decorative output rather than the strict target pattern.

GOAL: Move the plug right three times, then left once. CONTROLS: Click switches to set their cap and stem colors, defining the movement command. RULE: White cap with black stem moves right; black cap with white stem moves left. TRAP: Assuming white-white switches halt the program; they actually do nothing, allowing execution to continue.

GOAL: Align seven rotating glyphs to match specific target labels using a shared rotation cycle. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selection cursor; pressing the action button rotates the selected glyph forward or backward along the cycle. RULE: Each glyph belongs to a class where multiple visual states map to one label; find the minimal label index for each class to determine the shortest rotation path. TRAP: Assuming visual similarity implies identity; distinct glyphs may share the same class label, causing wasted rotations if you chase exact shapes instead of class equivalence.

GOAL: Move the yellow cross over its four dots, then switch to blue and cover its four dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active cross; Space switches between yellow and blue. RULE: A dot is cleared when the cross arm passes directly over it. TRAP: Thinking dots vanish permanently; they remain hidden under the cross arm, so don’t double-check coverage visually.

GOAL: Align the head with the blocks to match the target pattern. CONTROLS: Arrows move the head; extending the rod pushes or engulfs blocks. RULE: The rod only affects blocks when its final position overlaps them. TRAP: Believing blocks move when the rod leaves them; they remain frozen until pushed.

GOAL: Place all colored tiles into their matching slots to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Click a tile to select it, then click a target slot to swap them. Press space to confirm the solution. RULE: Direct swapping works between any two filled slots, allowing you to rotate pieces through a cycle efficiently. TRAP: Do not assume you need an empty space to move a piece; you can swap any two occupied positions directly.

GOAL: Fill seven empty slots on the red, green, and blue panels with the correct color tiles. CONTROLS: Click a color in the palette, then click an empty slot to place it. Press space to submit. RULE: Fill the panels in strict left-to-right order, treating each panel as a separate segment. TRAP: Trying to fill all slots on one panel before moving to the next breaks the sequence and fails.

GOAL: Place the yellow block into the matching yellow bracket at the top-left corner. CONTROLS: The red arrow rotates the ring counterclockwise; the green arrow rotates it clockwise. RULE: The ring consists of sixteen slots; rotating counterclockwise moves blocks toward the lower index positions. TRAP: Assuming the red arrow rotates clockwise wastes time, as it moves the yellow block away from the target bracket.

GOAL: Align colored tiles on a main panel with an attached sub-panel to form a continuous reading sequence. CONTROLS: Click palette items to select, click panel slots to place, and press space to validate. RULE: The connecting piece’s position dictates the order, ensuring the pre-filled sub-panel tile matches the sequence. TRAP: Assuming the connector can go anywhere; it must align with the sub-panel’s center to fix the reading order.

GOAL: Guide both blue tokens to meet at the top-center notch to complete the level. CONTROLS: Up and Down move both tokens vertically; Left and Right move them inward toward the center. RULE: Tokens slide together until hitting a wall or each other, requiring precise alignment to merge. TRAP: Believing tokens move independently wastes time; they always mirror each other’s horizontal movement.

GOAL: Transform the empty bottom-right panel to match the pattern logic derived from the three reference panels. CONTROLS: Click individual grid cells to toggle their color between blue and red. RULE: Each reference panel contains exactly four blue and four red cells; the solution must satisfy the hidden spatial relationship among them. TRAP: Do not assume clicking the central spinner rotates the ring; focus on changing the outer cell colors directly.

GOAL: Move the block to cover the plus marker. CONTROLS: Arrows slide the block; it glides until hitting a wall or obstacle. RULE: The block must fully overlap the target symbol to trigger success. TRAP: Believing you need to rotate the block; it only moves linearly.

GOAL: Turn specific blue squares orange to match the two dial patterns. CONTROLS: Click a square to switch its color between blue and orange. RULE: Each dial's white marks demand orange squares; grey marks demand blue squares. TRAP: Assuming every dial has equal white and grey marks; one dial here has five white marks.

GOAL: Clear the board by jumping pegs over neighbors into empty spaces. CONTROLS: Click a peg to select it, then click the highlighted target spot to jump. RULE: Each jump removes the jumped-over peg, reducing the total count by one. TRAP: The selected peg deselects after jumping; you must reselect it before every move.

GOAL: Guide the linkage tip to the ring center while positioning the bead correctly. CONTROLS: Clicking moves the linkage tip; clicking the gray pivot repositions the anchor point. RULE: The bead always sits at the midpoint between the pivot and the tip. TRAP: Assuming the pivot is fixed; it moves, allowing the bead to reach otherwise impossible spots.

GOAL: Align red pieces to match specific positions by inserting plugs to shift their reading order. CONTROLS: Click palette items to drag them into red or blue slots; press Space to submit the solution. RULE: Plugs inserted into red slots cause blue panels to be read in between, shifting the positions of remaining red pieces. TRAP: Assuming red pieces always appear first; plugs actually interleave blue panels, pushing later red pieces to the end of the sequence.

GOAL: Rotate specific rows and the left edge to move two yellow tiles into their target loops. CONTROLS: Green and red arrows rotated the left column or specific horizontal rows clockwise or counter-clockwise. RULE: Each click shifted tiles exactly one step along the loop; tracking tile positions after every move ensured targets were hit. TRAP: Assuming rotations affected all rows simultaneously wasted time; only the selected row or column moved, leaving others static.

GOAL: Arrange three colored sub-panels to match a nine-item target sequence. CONTROLS: Click palette items to select, then click slots to place; press space to submit. RULE: Red slots hold plugs that determine the order of the three sub-panels below. TRAP: Assuming sub-panels fill left-to-right regardless of which plug sits in the red slots.

GOAL: Rotate the grid to make all panels display the same color pattern as their matching center knobs. CONTROLS: Click a panel to rotate its eight surrounding cells clockwise. RULE: Shared cells belong to every panel they touch; changing one affects all connected rings. TRAP: Assuming a knob's ring maps directly to a fixed panel orientation; the pattern must match after rotation, not just by position.

GOAL: Arrange nested panels to match the target color sequence R,b,N,Y,N,b,R. CONTROLS: Drag colored tiles and plugs into empty panel slots to build the structure. RULE: Plug colors dictate which panel they connect; nested panels expand the reading order sequentially. TRAP: Assuming plugs can connect to any panel regardless of color match wastes moves and breaks the chain.

GOAL: Cover every colored dot with its matching shape to clear the level. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the cursor or active shape; spacebar confirms placement or toggles the current tool. RULE: Each shape covers all dots within a specific radius, not just the outline. TRAP: Assuming only the outer edge counts for coverage wastes time checking impossible boundary alignments.

GOAL: Merge two separated tokens into a single connected object. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the combined blob as one rigid unit. RULE: Once tokens touched, they fused into a single entity that moves together. TRAP: Assuming tokens moved independently after merging; trying to split them wasted moves.

GOAL: Slide blocks into matching colored brackets to clear the board. CONTROLS: Click side arrows to shift blocks left or right within their lanes. RULE: Blocks must land in brackets of the same color to complete the level. TRAP: Assuming any block fits any bracket; only color-matched placements count.

GOAL: Reposition three shapes to cover eight scattered dots using limited moves. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active shape’s center; Space cycles which shape is active. RULE: Shapes move in strict three-step increments, keeping centers aligned to a fixed grid. TRAP: Assuming shapes can stop anywhere wastes turns; they only halt on specific grid points.

GOAL: Make every panel’s ring match the hub color, with gray cells taking the third color. CONTROLS: Click a cell to cycle its color forward through blue, red, orange. RULE: Gray must become the color that is neither the hub’s nor the background. TRAP: Assuming gray always mirrors the hub; it does not, and that mismatch wastes clicks.

ESTABLISHED: Tokens freeze permanently if they overlap a ring, making ring walls impassable obstacles. FAILED: Moving the block into the right room failed to clear the level. GOAL IS NOT: Placing the block in the right room or pushing it against the ring. CONTROLS: Movement slides tokens until they hit a wall or overlap a ring, which freezes them instantly.

ESTABLISHED: Space resets the head to the start and clears the board. The head moves through empty space, not a grid. FAILED: Repeatedly pressing Down to reach the right side and pressing Space to reset did not clear the level. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the far right edge or clearing the screen. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the head. Space resets position and clears artifacts.

GOAL: Guide the yellow and orange blocks to their matching colored brackets. CONTROLS: Click the green or red arrows on the grid edges to slide entire rows or columns. RULE: Clicking an arrow shifts every block in that specific row or column one step in that direction. TRAP: Assuming blocks move independently; remember that moving one block often drags others along the same line.

GOAL: Move the head token into the target hole. CONTROLS: Click a token to make it the head. Arrows move the head. RULE: The ring structure does not block the head token. TRAP: Believing the ring blocks movement wastes time; the head can pass through.

GOAL: Rotate tokens to place yellow blocks inside the highlighted brackets. CONTROLS: Click top arrows to rotate the top row; click side arrows to rotate the connected lower track. RULE: The top row and lower track are independent cycles; side arrows do not affect the top row. TRAP: Assuming all arrows rotate a single continuous loop wastes moves trying to move yellow between disconnected sections.

GOAL: Align colored beads onto matching rings by repositioning anchor pieces. CONTROLS: Click empty space to park the cursor; click an anchor to swap its position with the cursor. RULE: A bead sits at the geometric center of its connected anchors, so moving one anchor shifts the bead. TRAP: Assuming beads move linearly with the cursor; they actually jump to new centroids, requiring precise anchor placement.

GOAL: Place the charcoal puppet onto the yellow target outline. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the black shape; the charcoal mirrors its horizontal movement. RULE: The pair reflects across a vertical axis, so move black to the mirror-image position of the target. TRAP: Moving black directly toward the yellow target pushes the charcoal away.

GOAL: Rotate the plug, move it down to align with the socket, then push it right until it clicks into place. CONTROLS: Arrows move the plug; Space rotates it. RULE: Move right until the plug stops automatically; the tips hit the pins without needing exact column counting. TRAP: Trying to calculate the exact stopping column wastes time; rely on the automatic collision stop instead.

GOAL: Align seven rotating glyph slots to match a target pattern within a strict action limit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the cursor between slots; UP and DOWN rotate the current glyph through its cycle. RULE: Each glyph follows a fixed seven-step cycle, so calculating the shortest rotation direction saves moves. TRAP: Assuming all slots share identical cycle orders without verifying exact bitmap matches caused wasted actions.

GOAL: Move the puppet to the yellow target while keeping the black shape on the right side of the divider. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active shape. Clicks transfer control between the black shape and the divider. RULE: The divider's position determines the puppet's horizontal mirror, so adjust the divider before final vertical moves. TRAP: Assuming the black shape must move right to align the puppet; actually, shifting the divider left reduces the required black movement.

GOAL: Move the plug four steps up. CONTROLS: Click demo cards to reveal movement patterns. RULE: Up requires caps on the top row and stems on the bottom row. TRAP: Assuming a single row controls all directions wastes time checking each card.

GOAL: Align six cycling glyphs to match a specific chain of target shapes. CONTROLS: Up and Down arrows rotate the selected glyph through its cycle; Left and Right arrows move between slots. RULE: All slots share one seven-state cycle, allowing you to calculate the shortest rotation path to the target. TRAP: Assuming glyphs differ per slot; recognizing the shared cycle prevents redundant probing and wasted actions.

ESTABLISHED: Two static red ingots sit on the right. White outlines around them vanished permanently after the first click. The central divider is a dashed, passable line. FAILED: Toggling the red piece to vertical and back did not restore the outlines. Moving the left machine pieces did not alter the ingots or the divider. GOAL IS NOT: Matching the ingots' color to the left pieces, or filling the vanished white outlines with the machine parts. CONTROLS: Clicking a piece toggles its orientation. Clicking the ingot area removed the hint outlines immediately.

GOAL: Move three yellow snowflakes to their matching brackets. CONTROLS: Click OUT arrows to push flakes outward; click ROT arrows to spin them around the center. RULE: Each arrow affects only the snowflake in its specific lane, so you can solve each one independently. TRAP: Assuming rotations affect all flakes simultaneously led to unnecessary moves; they only spin the flake in that specific arm.

ESTABLISHED: Pouring at 0° paints the top half. The canvas is not liquid; it is a swept band overwrite. The goal is not to match the panel's colors directly. FAILED: Pressing Down at 0° tilt did nothing. Testing liquid pooling failed. Matching the panel's specific color arrangement failed. GOAL IS NOT: Matching the panel's colors. Creating a liquid pool. CONTROLS: Left/Right tilts the source. Up/Down are currently no-ops. Space pours paint.

ESTABLISHED: The sprite stays on one horizontal row and moves only left or right. The maze regenerates periodically, changing layout while keeping the sprite’s position. Green blocks are destructible by clicking, using a limited budget. A pink target appears in later waves but has remained static for several actions. FAILED: Clicking green blocks did not remove the maze barrier to the target. Waiting for regeneration did not align the corridor with the sprite’s row. Moving the sprite horizontally did not reach the pink target. GOAL IS NOT: Reaching the pink target by walking directly to it, as

GOAL: Cover all yellow targets using two black pieces and a movable divider. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected piece or divider; clicks select them. RULE: The divider reflects pieces to create puppets; both real pieces and puppets must cover targets. TRAP: Moving the divider first can block clicks on pieces below it; select pieces before shifting the barrier.

GOAL: Align yellow tiles with their target brackets. CONTROLS: Arrows shifted connected tile groups in cycles. RULE: Shared corner tiles linked row and column movements, allowing independent phase adjustments. TRAP: Assuming all connected tiles move as a single rigid block.

GOAL: Rotate each tile's symbol to match its required target class. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the cursor between tiles; pressing UP or DOWN cycles the current tile's symbol. RULE: Match every tile to its specific assigned symbol class to complete the level. TRAP: Assuming a fixed number of presses per tile wastes actions; instead, verify the symbol after every press.

GOAL: Move block B2 left and down to align its puppet with target Y2. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected block; clicks select a block to receive dots. RULE: A block’s puppet mirrors its movement, so moving B2 down pushes its puppet up into place. TRAP: Assuming the action bar’s orange section indicated failure rather than usage led to hesitation.

GOAL: The level required merging two separate tokens into a single Y-shape to reach the target zone. CONTROLS: Clicking a location moved any token within range toward that spot. RULE: Tokens within the same click radius merged into a combined shape, allowing one move to position both parts. TRAP: Believing each token must be moved individually wastes actions; merging them early saves clicks but risks collision if timed poorly.

GOAL: Clear Level 3 by moving all pieces to their targets within twelve actions. CONTROLS: Clicking a piece selects it as the active tip; clicking an empty spot moves it there. RULE: The bead always sits at the exact midpoint of the two pieces, so moves must keep this center in open space. TRAP: Assuming you can move pieces independently; the bead’s position links them, so one piece’s move forces the other’s relative position.

GOAL: Guide the four-cell tip through the shrinking gray corridor to reach the head. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the entire tip block four cells in that direction. RULE: Each move consumes fuel; the tip cannot enter black or empty space. TRAP: Assuming the path remains open after you pass; the gray turns black behind you, blocking return routes.

GOAL: Cover all yellow areas by positioning the piece so its reflection puppets fill the remaining gaps. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the piece or axes; clicks grabbed pieces or toggled mirror axes. RULE: Mirrors compose; moving axes generated multiple reflected copies of the piece simultaneously. TRAP: Assuming only direct placement mattered, ignoring how axis adjustments created hidden reflected copies needed for full coverage.

GOAL: Reach the exit without being caught by the patrolling guards. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move one tile per press; each move costs energy from the bottom bar. RULE: Guards spot you only if they face your direction; turning away hides you. TRAP: Assuming the bar shows time remaining; it actually tracks distance, so wandering wastes energy and causes failure.

GOAL: Align all knob colors to match the center hub. CONTROLS: Click a special knob to flip its surrounding cells; click normal knobs for no effect. RULE: Only special knobs change the board state; normal knobs are inert placeholders. TRAP: Misidentifying grid coordinates for pixel positions caused wasted clicks on empty background gaps.

GOAL: Route the sky beam to the target by clearing its path. CONTROLS: Click left to shrink, right to grow. RULE: Objects merge when touching, blocking movement until separated. TRAP: Assuming gray blocks stay independent; they merged, trapping the beam.

GOAL: Place four tokens into the matching ring sockets to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Click a token to select it, then use arrow keys to slide it one step. RULE: Tokens only stop when they hit a wall or a socket, sliding until blocked. TRAP: Assuming you can stop mid-slide; you must plan paths that end exactly at the hole, as overshooting requires long detours.

GOAL: Navigate the grid to the center while avoiding moving guards. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move one step; waiting is allowed but costs an action. RULE: Guards patrol fixed paths and reverse at walls; you cannot share a cell with a guard at any step. TRAP: Assuming you can cross a guard’s path instantly; you must wait for the guard to clear the intersection before moving.

GOAL: Slide the divider to reveal hidden yellow patterns and align them with the hook’s puppets. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active element; clicks confirm or reset the current selection. RULE: Yellow regions are only counted if they are fully uncovered by the vertical divider. TRAP: Assuming the divider’s position was static; failing to shift it left first left critical yellow cells permanently hidden.

GOAL: Grow the tip, then walk to the head within 13 moves. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the bar; clicks set the fire pattern; RIGHT positioned the bar. RULE: The plus pattern shrank in L1, so it likely grew the tip here; column patterns fired rays. TRAP: Assuming any fire pattern works; using a column pattern fired a useless ray instead of growing the tip.

GOAL: Position the floating bead precisely into the target ring. CONTROLS: Click empty map slots to move the bead to their midpoint. RULE: The bead always settles at the average coordinate of the two selected slots. TRAP: Assuming the bead moves directly to the clicked slot; it actually jumps to the center point between the previous and new slot locations.

GOAL: Arrange five colored blocks into their target slots without overlapping. CONTROLS: Click side buttons to shrink or grow each color’s length. RULE: A block’s position shifts as it changes size; order operations to avoid collisions. TRAP: Assuming shrinking one block leaves its neighbors untouched; they often shift and block others.

GOAL: Position yellow tiles under dividers to cover all yellow cells. CONTROLS: Arrows move the currently selected divider; clicks select a new divider or piece. RULE: Only the selected element responds to arrow keys; clicking switches focus instantly. TRAP: Assuming pieces move with dividers; they are static unless explicitly clicked and moved.

GOAL: Merge four M-tokens into a large shape covering the ball. CONTROLS: Clicks move nearby tokens toward the cursor; close tokens merge automatically. RULE: Clicks attract tokens within a fixed radius, pulling distant pieces closer for merging. TRAP: Believing clicks only affect the nearest token; they simultaneously pull multiple pieces, causing unintended shifts.

GOAL: Navigate the plug to the target socket by shrinking it and moving left and down. CONTROLS: Toggle switches to encode movement: Left (stem1+stem3), Down (cap1+stem1), Shrink (cap1+stem2). RULE: Specific switch combinations trigger distinct actions, verified by observing the plug’s animation response. TRAP: Assuming symmetrical controls for opposite directions wastes time; Left requires two stems while Right uses one.

GOAL: Recolor two shapes by touching matching blocks. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the active shape. Space switched which shape was active. RULE: A shape changed color only when its arm touched a block of that color. TRAP: The health bar did not drop every move, causing wasted time guessing the timer's logic.

GOAL: Collect every red item while avoiding the moving enemy guards. CONTROLS: Use the arrow keys to move the character one step in that direction. RULE: You can only occupy a square when it is empty; the guard’s path changes each turn. TRAP: Assuming you can cross a guard’s path safely; you must wait for them to move away first.

GOAL: Move the bead to absorb specific colored discs in sequence. CONTROLS: Click a slot, then click a new location to move it; the bead follows the average position. RULE: The bead’s position is always the exact center of the three slots, allowing precise targeting. TRAP: Assuming absorbed discs remain visible; they vanish, leaving only the bead’s updated colors to confirm success.

GOAL: Navigate the grid to the exit without triggering hidden traps. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move one step in the chosen direction. RULE: Red enemies kill on contact, so route around them carefully. TRAP: Assuming all paths are safe; a single wrong step into a danger zone causes failure.

GOAL: Fit the small plug into the large socket by matching its shape and color. CONTROLS: Click grid columns to add instructions: Rotate turns it, Recolor changes hue, Down moves it, Grow doubles size. RULE: The plug must rotate first so its notch faces down, aligning perfectly with the socket’s bump after growing. TRAP: Thinking rotation order doesn’t matter. Rotating after growing misaligns the notch, causing a collision.

ESTABLISHED: Yellow is fixed, not floating. Buttons exist only on W1, W3, and W4; W2 has none. FAILED: Clicking W2 wall sections. Assuming yellow floats with water. Searching for hidden W2 buttons. GOAL IS NOT: Triggering W2 via its walls. Using yellow as a water gauge. CONTROLS: Buttons at row 61 pump specific pools. Walls block flow. White background is empty space.

GOAL: Guide the dot to the target by moving bars and clearing the path. CONTROLS: Click bars to shrink or grow them, shifting their position and length. RULE: Shrink obstacles to create gaps, then grow the dot’s bar to reach the goal. TRAP: Believing the dot moves automatically; you must manually extend the bar to land on the target.
ESTABLISHED: The target assembly fits visually. FAILED: None. GOAL IS NOT: Unknown. CONTROLS: Click to select; arrows move pieces freely through overlaps.

GOAL: Move the plug right four times, then up twice. CONTROLS: Click cards to read binary codes; click grid bits to set moves; press play to run. RULE: The left panel displays the selected card's code, revealing that RIGHT is 010000 and UP is 100001. TRAP: Assuming directional codes follow a simple pattern wastes time; LEFT and UP differ by only one bit.

ESTABLISHED: The patroller moves predictably along a fixed loop. FAILED: Waiting for an opening or trying to outrun the patroller directly. GOAL IS NOT: A specific tile that is currently guarded or unreachable by the patroller. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player; one move per turn; the patroller moves simultaneously.

GOAL: Clear Level 6 by rotating the blue piece to point right. CONTROLS: Click the blue plus sign to rotate its orientation. RULE: Rotations skip blocked directions, cycling to the next valid one. TRAP: Assuming rotations strictly follow visual order, ignoring obstacles.

GOAL: Fill two separate balls simultaneously using a single shrinking token and a chasing ring. CONTROLS: Click anywhere to move the token away from the click point, causing the ring to pursue it. RULE: The ring must overlap the ball to count as filling it, allowing the token to fill the other ball. TRAP: Believing the ring destroys the token or ball on contact, causing unnecessary avoidance instead of strategic overlap.

ESTABLISHED: Orange moves via corridor to right corner. Pegs block entry into panels A and B. FAILED: Moving right into pegs does nothing; pegs did not move or disappear. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the corridor end or triggering a standard peg jump. CONTROLS: Right moves orange. Up moves orange. Left moves orange. No pushing observed on dead pegs.

ESTABLISHED: The grid uses a four-pixel cell size with a two-pixel offset, creating a fifteen-by-fifteen maze. Tokens occupy full cells while dots are centered within them. FAILED: Assuming a three-pixel offset or treating dots as full-cell obstacles blocked movement and connectivity checks. GOAL IS NOT: Moving a token into a cell containing a dot, as dots block the path entirely. CONTROLS: Tokens move four pixels in a direction only if the entire target four-by-four cell is black.

ESTABLISHED: Three cup fills are required to win. FAILED: Filling only two cups triggers a failure flash. GOAL IS NOT: Surviving ceiling collisions; hitting the ceiling causes immediate failure.
